a: F = ma — force equals mass times acceleration.
For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
V = IR — voltage equals current times resistance.
E = mc² relates energy and mass; c is speed of light.
v = fλ — wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.
p = mv — momentum equals mass times velocity.
W = F·d (force times displacement in the direction of the force).
P = W/t = Fv — power is work per time.
ρ = m/V — density equals mass over volume.
P = F/A — pressure equals force over area.
F = k|q1 q2|/r² — electrostatic force between point charges.
n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2 for refraction.
ΔU = Q - W — change in internal energy equals heat added minus work done by the system.
Entropy measures disorder or the number of microscopic configurations; isolated systems tend to increase entropy.
